asyntis.name: ASYNTIS GmbH
asyntis.identified_as: ASYNTIS GmbH, Putzbrunn (Solalinden, near Munich); Amtsgericht München HRB 139903
asyntis.identification_basis: Earlybird's own release of 2002-07-31 (release 195): 'Earlybird investiert zwei Millionen Euro in den Semiconductor Spezialisten ASYNTIS GmbH', partner Hendrik Brandis joined the board. The register (North Data) also shows Earlybird GmbH & Co. KG Parallel-Beteiligungskommanditgesellschaft III as shareholder. The hint 'optical components' is wrong: plasma etch equipment for thin wafers.

entry.quote: has raised € 2 million in its first round of financing with Earlybird
entry.entry_asserted: The firm's release calls it the company's 'first round of financing'; the company was founded in 2001 (registered 20 Nov 2001) and the September 2003 release calls Earlybird the 'existing investor'. No Series letter and no Seed label on record.

asyntis.status_detail: Insolvency proceedings opened by Amtsgericht München on 25 January 2006 (Az. 1506 IN 256/06); company in liquidation April 2006, proceedings closed 24 October 2008, struck off June 2009. No asset sale or successor found (looked in the firm's press archive, VentureCapital Magazin's index and the register page only).

valuation.basis: No priced figure of USD 1B or more; two rounds of EUR 2M and EUR 4M, then insolvency.

asyntis.notes: Maker of plasma etch (dry etch stress relief) equipment for thin semiconductor wafers, founded 2001, product line SILICON STAR. Entry is an unnamed first round (Earlybird alone, EUR 2M); the record names no Seed or Series letter, so graduation is left null although a EUR 4M second round led by AdAstra followed in September 2003.

europroteome.name: Europroteome AG
europroteome.identified_as: Europroteome AG, Hennigsdorf (near Berlin); Amtsgericht Neuruppin HRB 5784
europroteome.identification_basis: Earlybird's release of 2002-02-05 (release 157) names its 2001 investment in 'Europroteome, a oncology company'; the company's own release of 2003-07-01 says its 2001 VC consortium was 'angeführt von Earlybird Venture Capital und Heidelberg Innovation' and quotes Earlybird's Rolf Mathies. The register (North Data) shows both Earlybird KG III and Parallel KG III as shareholders in fund accounts up to 2014.

entry.quote: ein starkes Konsortium von VCs zu formen - angeführt von Earlybird Venture Capital und Heidelberg Innovation
entry.entry_asserted: The company's release of 01.07.2003 is headed 'EUROPROTEOME AG erweitert A-Runden Finanzierung' and dates the consortium led by Earlybird and Heidelberg Innovation to 2001; Earlybird's Rolf Mathies says there 'Seit zwei Jahren verfolgen wir nun die Entwicklung' and speaks of 'Unsere initiale Investmenthypothese'. Earlybird's own release of 05.02.2002 lists Europroteome among its 2001 investments. Month not on record (the firm's portfolio page is first captured 2001-10-05). The company was founded in 1997, so this A round was not its first money: BioWorld calls it the 'second financing round'.

rounds.round: investment named in the firm's review of 2001 (round not named there)

rounds.note: Amount and 'second financing round' are from the search-result snippet of this BioWorld item only; the page itself returned 403 to curl and WebFetch, so it was NOT loaded. Lead investors and the 'A-Runde' label are confirmed on the loaded bionity page.

europroteome.status_detail: Filed for insolvency in August 2004 (BioCentury, 18 August 2004: 'has filed for insolvency'). The register entry lived on until it was struck off on 12 June 2014; Earlybird's fund III accounts still listed the shareholding up to the year 2014. No asset sale or successor found.

valuation.basis: No priced figure of USD 1B or more; the 2001 round was about EUR 9.5M (snippet only) and the company went insolvent in 2004.

europroteome.notes: 'The Human Cancer Company': proteomics on a large human tumour sample bank to find cancer markers and targets, founded 1997, bought phase-it intelligent Solutions AG in February 2003. Entry is the 2001 round the company itself calls its A round, co-led by Earlybird and Heidelberg Innovation; the EUR 9.5M figure rests on an unloadable BioWorld page. Second register citation for the status: https://www.northdata.com/Europroteome%20AG,%20Hennigsdorf/Amtsgericht%20Neuruppin%20HRB%205784

internetwork.name: interNetwork AG
internetwork.identified_as: interNetwork AG, Wiesbaden (HRB 11261); US arm interNetwork, Inc., San Francisco
internetwork.identification_basis: Earlybird's own release dated 2002-04-04 (release 202): 'Target Partners und Earlybird investieren 5 Millionen Euro in den Software-Spezialisten interNetwork AG'; a second release of 2003-11-05 (release 266) reports the follow-on.

entry.quote: Target Partners und Earlybird investieren 5 Millionen Euro in den Software-Spezialisten interNetwork AG
entry.entry_asserted: The firm's release of 05.11.2003 says of the EUR 3M second round: 'Beide Fonds hatten bereits in der ersten Runde investiert' (https://index.commoncrawl.org/CC-MAIN-2008-2009-index?url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.earlybird.com%2Fde%2Fpress%2Frelease%2F266%2F&output=json). The April 2002 release itself gives no Series letter and no Seed label; the company was founded in February 1999 and already had customers such as Deutsche Telekom and Nortel.

rounds.round: first round (named so in the 2003 release)

internetwork.status_detail: Preliminary insolvency administrator appointed by Amtsgericht Wiesbaden on 26 April 2005 (Az. 10 IN 263/05); in liquidation from July 2005; struck off for lack of assets on 6 January 2011. No asset sale or successor found.

valuation.basis: No priced figure of USD 1B or more; two rounds of EUR 5M and EUR 3M, then insolvency.

internetwork.notes: Software-based load testing and monitoring for IP and telecom networks (product sm@rtTEST / smartTest), founded February 1999 in Wiesbaden; by late 2003 it presented itself as 'interNetwork AG in San Francisco und Wiesbaden' with a US CEO. The legal entity and register seat stayed in Wiesbaden, so the HQ is given as Wiesbaden. Entry is an unnamed first round led by Target Partners.

intime.name: InTime Software, Inc.
intime.identified_as: InTime Software, Inc., Cupertino (California; Delaware corporation, SEC CIK 1262784)
intime.identification_basis: Earlybird's own release of 2001-12-10 (release 208), headline only: 'Earlybird investiert in InTime Software, Inc. - InTime schließt $14 Mio. Finanzierungsrunde', contacts Steve Ciesinski (Palo Alto) and Hendrik Brandis. The body was a PDF that is not in the archive.

entry.quote: Earlybird investiert in InTime Software, Inc. - InTime schließt $14 Mio. Finanzierungsrunde
entry.entry_asserted: Not asserted in words. The firm's headline announces the investment together with the USD 14M round, the form its releases use for new investments, and no earlier release names InTime; the firm's portfolio page for it is first captured in June 2002. The round carries no name (no Series letter) in any page loaded: the round stays null. It was not the company's first money (USD 5.5M of private funding by May 2000).

rounds.round: private funding (unnamed; total raised to date)
rounds.lead: Haywood Securities, The Angels Forum and private investors

rounds.round: Unattributed VC (investors listed: Cadence, Earlybird Venture, Novus Ventures, Walden Venture Capital)
Regulation D notice of sale (paper filing, amount not readable online)

intime.status_detail: No sale found; the company lapsed. California registration (branch of the Delaware corporation, 10131 Bubb Road, Cupertino): Secretary of State forfeiture 13 Jan 2005, agent for service resigned 2 Sep 2005, Franchise Tax Board forfeiture 2 Apr 2007, status 'Forfeited'; the Texas registration was forfeited for tax on 11 Feb 2005 (https://opencorporates.com/companies/us_tx/0800058389). In September 2003 the founder spun out Giga Scale Integration (later Chip Estimate) with the Time Architect tool; EE Times, 29.09.2003 (https://www.eetimes.com/?p=1146759): 'InTime retains no ownership in the new company', so that is not a sale of InTime.

valuation.basis: No priced figure of USD 1B or more; largest round USD 14M.

intime.notes: Chip-design (EDA) software: RTL timing analysis and floor planning (Time Architect, Time Planner, Time Director), founded January 1999 by ex-Cadence CTO George Janac. The firm's release gives only date and amount, so the entry round is unnamed (null). Status rests on state registers mirrored by OpenCorporates, not on a shutdown notice; the exact end date is not on record (the CFO left in December 2002, a Reg D sale was filed in September 2003, the registrations lapsed in 2005). The pipeline's weak CIK join (INTIME SOFTWARE INC, 1262784) is the right company.

iq.name: IQ Labs
iq.identified_as: IQ Labs, Incorporated, Hayward (California corporation no. 2008285)
iq.identification_basis: Earlybird's own release of 2001-05-15 (release 224): 'Earlybird gibt Investment in IQ Labs bekannt', 'its investment in the Series D of Hayward, Calif.-based IQ Labs'; partner Steve Ciesinski joined the board. Not iQ wireless and not IQ Power.

entry.quote: today announced its investment in the Series D of Hayward, Calif.-based IQ Labs
entry.entry_asserted: The firm's release: 'We're pleased to welcome IQ Labs to our portfolio as our latest investment in the U.S.' and 'Pursuant to the financing, Ciesinski has been elected to the Board'. Co-investors named: Draper Fisher Jurvetson and Draper Richards. No amount and no lead on record.

iq.status_detail: No sale or shutdown notice found; the company lapsed. California register (IQ LABS, INCORPORATED, 3556 Investment Blvd, Hayward): Secretary of State suspension 5 Mar 2002, revived 20 Aug 2002, suspended again 13 Jan 2005, Franchise Tax Board suspension 1 Aug 2011; status 'Suspended'. Restated articles of 23 Apr 2001 fit the Series D. The firm's portfolio page for it is last captured in March 2003.

valuation.basis: No priced figure of USD 1B or more; no round amount on record.

iq.notes: Enterprise software that automates provisioning and change management of a company's telecom and data-communication resources (founder and CEO Farzad Naimi). Earlybird came in at the Series D. Status rests on the California register as mirrored by OpenCorporates; when it actually stopped trading (between 2003 and 2005) is not on record. The pipeline's weak CIK join for this row (IQ SOFTWARE CORP, CIK 886167) is a different company: IQ Software Corp of Norcross, Georgia, deregistered in 1998. Drop that join.

iscribe.name: iScribe
iscribe.identification_basis: Earlybird's own press release of 2001-04-17 (release 210): iScribe closed a $15M Series D 'Led by new investor Earlybird'; Earlybird partner Vera Kallmeyer joined the board.

entry.quote: Led by new investor Earlybird, and joined by previous investors Kleiner Perkins Caufield and Byers, Galen Partners, Domain Associates
entry.entry_asserted: The firm's release calls Earlybird the 'new investor' leading the Series D, against the 'previous investors' named beside it.

iscribe.status_detail: AdvancePCS bought iScribe's software code and other assets in December 2001 (asset purchase; price not stated in the 10-K). AdvancePCS itself was bought by Caremark Rx in 2004.

valuation.basis: No priced figure of USD 1B or more; the last round was USD 15M and the sale was an asset purchase.

iscribe.notes: Handheld electronic prescribing for physicians, founded January 1999. Earlybird entered late, leading the Series D; eight months later AdvancePCS bought the code and assets (10-K for fiscal 2002: 'In December 2001, we purchased software code and other assets of iScribe'). The sale was of code and assets, not of the corporation (its California registration was forfeited in October 2002, https://opencorporates.com/companies/us_ca/2134507); it is given as acquired because the business passed to AdvancePCS, as in the Kleiner Perkins sibling row.

music-united.name: Music-United.com AG
music-united.identification_basis: The register, as read by North Data: the accounts of Earlybird GmbH & Co. KG Parallel-Beteiligungskommanditgesellschaft III (published 9 June 2021, 15 shareholdings) list Music-United.com AG, shown on the company's page as 'Shareholder: Earlybird GmbH & Co. KG Parallel-Beteiligungskommanditgesellschaft III'. Together with the firm's own page /portfolio/investment/music_united.html (captured March 2001). No press article or firm release naming Earlybird's round was found.
music-united.status_detail: Preliminary insolvency administrator appointed by Amtsgericht Hamburg on 1 October 2001 (Az. 67e IN 211/01); in liquidation; struck off for lack of assets (register notice of 30 January 2004). No asset sale or successor found.

valuation.basis: No priced figure of USD 1B or more; no round amount on record, insolvent within about 18 months of launch.

music-united.notes: Hamburg music portal launched in April 2000 (mood-based music search engines, editorial content, later ticketing with CTS Eventim and CD sales with Primusmedia; Horizont 15.01.2001, https://www.horizont.net/medien/nachrichten/-Music-united.com-steigt-ins-Ticketing-ein-27426, and 02.02.2001, https://www.horizont.net/medien/nachrichten/-Music-united.com-baut-sein-Angebot-aus-27891; neither names an investor). The holding vehicle is an Earlybird III fund, so the money went in between the portal's 2000 start and the March 2001 capture, but no source names the round, date or amount: entry null. Searched: the firm's press archive (no hit for 'music' before 2009), Horizont's search, VentureCapital Magazin's index, Bing News, one WebSearch.

vital-sensors.name: Vital Sensors, Inc.
vital-sensors.identified_as: Vital Sensors, Inc., Richmond (Virginia); holding Vital Sensors Holding Company, Inc. (Delaware); German operating subsidiary Vital Sensors GmbH, Hannover (HRB 60781)
vital-sensors.identification_basis: WEAK, read this: no firm release, press article or filing naming Earlybird as its investor could be loaded. What ties them: (1) Earlybird's own site carried the page /portfolio/recent/vital_sensors/ from 2006-04-07 to 2007-09-11 (index only, body not read; https://web.archive.org/web/20060512123737/http://www.earlybird.com/de/portfolio/recent/vital_sensors/); (2) the only companies of that name are this Richmond medical-device company and its Hannover subsidiary, registered on 7 March 2006, one month before the first capture; (3) two vendor pages, both loaded, list Earlybird among its investors (CB Insights: 'Earlybird Venture' beside Golden Angels Network, CNF Investments, Stratus Ventures, iNetworks; Preqin: 'iNetworks, Earlybird, CNF Investments'). Vendor pages are not citable for stage or status; they are the only text naming Earlybird.

rounds.round: Angel, Angel II, Angel III, Angel IV (four rounds, amounts not shown)

vital-sensors.status_detail: No sale found. The German operating company Vital Sensors GmbH, Hannover (research, development and production of the sensor systems) got a preliminary insolvency administrator on 29 August 2013 (Amtsgericht Hannover, 907 IN 649/13), was in liquidation from November 2013 and was struck off in July 2019. The US parent Vital Sensors, Inc. (800 E Leigh St, Richmond) is 'Inactive' in the Virginia register as mirrored by OpenCorporates (https://opencorporates.com/companies/us_va/06427090); its end date is not shown. A Cytomedix proxy of October 2014 still names it as a private Richmond company with a CNF Investments director on its board.

valuation.basis: No priced figure of USD 1B or more; vendor total raised USD 3.6M (not citable).

vital-sensors.membership_detail: Not flagged not_found because the firm's own site listed a company of this name and two vendor pages name Earlybird as an investor of the Richmond company; but no round with Earlybird in it is on record anywhere I could read. If the judge wants a first-party or press source in words, this row has none.
vital-sensors.notes: Implantable telemetric pressure sensor for monitoring heart-failure patients, founded 2002 (vendor), based in the Virginia BioTechnology Research Park in Richmond with development in Hannover. Entry round, date and amount are unknown: null. CB Insights (vendor) also says it bought 'Mesotec' on 2006-09-01; I could not confirm that or any link between Mesotec and Earlybird in the register, so no sale_consideration flag. Searched: the firm's press archive (no hit), EDGAR full text (41 hits, none naming Earlybird; no Form D), Bing News, two WebSearches (vendor pages only), North Data, OpenCorporates.
